content: 1. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored when these drugs are coadministered. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 4. When mavorixafor is coadministered with P-glycoprotein inhibitors, its levels should be monitored, and the dose reduced if necessary. 5. Atazanavir and medroxyprogesterone may decrease each other's effects by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are advised, and alternatives should be considered if available. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, as methadone dosage may require modification. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels of meperidine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Atazanavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 10. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 12. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Atazanavir enhances the effects of metoprolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, and the mifepristone dose should not exceed 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If coadministration is necessary, specific dose adjustments for mifepristone are required based on the patient's current dose. 19. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 20. Atazanavir decreases the effects of miglitol through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Atazanavir and mipomersen may increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, with liver function tests (LFTs) recommended due to the potential for increased hepatic enzymes. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of mirvetuximab soravtansine, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 24. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Mitotane decreases the levels of atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Dosage adjustments may be necessary when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled) by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels of mometasone (inhaled) by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity, including the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mometasone (intranasal) by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of mometasone (intranasal) by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Atazanavir enhances the effects of nadolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Caution and monitoring are advised, and lowering the beta-blocker dose should be considered. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels of naldemedine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised, with monitoring for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-glycoprotein inhibitors. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels of naldemedine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, with monitoring for potential adverse effects if coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Atazanavir decreases the effects of nateglinide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 35. Atazanavir enhances the effects of nebivolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended, and lowering the beta-blocker dose should be considered. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, although no dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 41. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, although no dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 42. Atazanavir and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, and dosage adjustments of nilotinib may be necessary. Refer to nilotinib prescribing information for dosing instructions. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. 48. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated, with monitoring for increased adverse events. 49. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norelgesteromin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, and alternatives should be considered if available. 51. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norethindrone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, and alternatives should be considered if available. 52. Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate may decrease each other's effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, and alternatives should be considered if available. 53. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norgestimate by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended, and alternatives should be considered if available. 54. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. 55. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. 56. Atazanavir increases the levels of nortriptyline through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline through other mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are recommended, with careful titration of the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, including using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitoring its response during coadministration with tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and cobicistat. 57. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Close monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is advised, with subsequent dose titration as needed. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 58. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Close monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is advised, with subsequent dose titration as needed. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 59. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Close monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is advised, with subsequent dose titration as needed. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 60. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir (DSC) by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Increased levels of paritaprevir occur when coadministered with atazanavir/ritonavir; administer atazanavir 300 mg (without ritonavir) in the morning when coadministered with Viekira Pak. 61. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 62. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. 63. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 64. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 65. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat, a CYP3A4 substrate, by half when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 66. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the dose of osilodrostat, a CYP3A4 substrate, by half when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 67. Atazanavir increases the levels of ospemifene by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
